guard: new defaults can create channels, byte-exact legacy defaults upgrade, user-edited personas remain untouched, and a minted credential's lifetime and identity are the operator's flags, not the command's defaults
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/workspace build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli typecheck && pnpm smoke:persona-templates && pnpm smoke:mint-provision:auth
why: Setup writes the default persona from a literal template rather than through the guarded agent-file writer.
The mutation is compile-clean and restores the shipped regression: an empty default post ACL under the protocol's default-deny policy.
The cells check the new-install grant and both sides of the byte-exact migration decision without touching real setup state.

mutations.name: M1 remove the default wildcard post grant
mutations.expectRed: default-channel-creation: default stays unsubscribed with wildcard read and post ACLs
mutations.cell: default-channel-creation: default stays unsubscribed with wildcard read and post ACLs
mutations.note: This is the exact shipped regression. Typecheck remains green, then the static template assertion observes that a fresh default can no longer create or post to a concrete channel.

mutations.name: M2 stop recognizing the byte-exact legacy default
mutations.expectRed: legacy-default-upgrade: the byte-exact legacy template gains wildcard post permission
mutations.cell: legacy-default-upgrade: the byte-exact legacy template gains wildcard post permission
mutations.note: This restores the upgrade-path defect while compiling cleanly: an untouched legacy default remains post-denied after setup reruns.

mutations.name: M3 migrate every existing default regardless of user edits
mutations.expectRed: edited-default-preservation: a user-edited legacy persona stays byte-identical
mutations.cell: edited-default-preservation: a user-edited legacy persona stays byte-identical
mutations.note: This broadens the repair decision past byte equality. The preservation cell detects that an edited persona would be overwritten.

mutations.name: M4 drift the frozen legacy fixture to the current wildcard post grant
mutations.expectRed: legacy-migration-fixture: the frozen legacy template carries the empty post ACL
mutations.cell: legacy-migration-fixture: the frozen legacy template carries the empty post ACL
mutations.note: A future current-template edit must not redefine which prior-release bytes are eligible. This compile-clean mutation makes the frozen fixture cease representing the shipped empty-post default.

mutations.name: M5 remove workflow capability from the setup default
mutations.expectRed: default-workflow-capability: the default declares spawn and run
mutations.cell: default-workflow-capability: the default declares spawn and run
mutations.note: Restores the spawn-only default; the real setup subprocess also checks the parsed on-disk capabilities.

mutations.name: M6 drop the mint lifetime before it reaches the seam
mutations.expectRed: the JWT's exp is iat + the flag, computed within the command's own second
mutations.cell: the JWT's exp is iat + the flag, computed within the command's own second
mutations.note: Restores the shipped half 1: the flag parses and validates but never reaches mintCreds, so the mint itself still succeeds while the credential stays unbounded (exp undefined). The success cell stays green by design; the exp-arithmetic cell is the one that catches the dropped lifetime.

mutations.name: M7 churn the identity on every re-mint
mutations.expectRed: the re-minted credential's principal IS the original's (same nkey, so every durable keyed to it survives)
mutations.cell: the re-minted credential's principal IS the original's (same nkey, so every durable keyed to it survives)
mutations.note: Restores the shipped half 2: --identity is read and validated, then ignored, so the re-minted credential is a new principal and every durable keyed to the old one is orphaned.

mutations.name: M8 stop refusing a TTL the seam would refuse
mutations.expectRed: --expires-in 0 exits 1 naming the value (a TTL the seam would refuse)
mutations.cell: --expires-in 0 exits 1 naming the value (a TTL the seam would refuse)
mutations.note: Drops the CLI-side validation so a zero TTL falls through to the seam's throw after the operator believed the mint was underway. The cell requires the refusal at the command surface, naming the value.
